canonical_master.interpretation: The canonical master remains genus-level. Species-resolved records must not be silently generalized across Taraxacum.

records.citation: Iftime A, Iftime O. 2012. Diet of Testudo graeca in Romania.
records.plant_part: young leaves; flowers/inflorescences may be ingested with leaves
supports: Wild T. g. ibera directly consumed Taraxacum material.
Taraxacum was among frequently consumed young-leaf plant taxa in the observed population.
does_not_support: daily, unlimited, staple, or nutritionally complete status

records.citation: Mitrevichin Z. 2023. Notes on the diet of Testudo hermanni boettgeri and T. graeca ibera in south-western Bulgaria.
supports: Independent direct observation of wild T. g. ibera feeding on Taraxacum sp.

records.citation: Muñoz A, Soler J, Martínez-Silvestre A. 2009. Aportaciones al estudio de la alimentación de Testudo hermanni hermanni en el Parque Natural de la Sierra de Montsant. Boletín de la Asociación Herpetológica Española 20:54-58.
records.study_type: wild/semi-natural feeding context plus fecal-diet study
supports: The 2009 paper explicitly describes direct observations in free and large semi-natural enclosure Hermann's tortoises showing a high tendency to ingest Taraxacum officinale.
records.source_id_note: Legacy identifier retained for linkage stability; the verified publication is Muñoz, Soler & Martínez-Silvestre 2009, not a 2008 Soler/Martínez paper.

records.citation: Plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 concentrations in Hermann's tortoises exposed to natural sunlight and artificial UV sources. AJVR 2012;73(11):1781.
records.study_type: controlled UV study; diet was background husbandry, not a food-safety trial
supports: T. officinale was included in a mixed diet used for captive Hermann's tortoises in a veterinary study.

records.citation: Bielli M, Nardini G, Di Girolamo N, Savarino P. 2015. Hematological values for adult eastern Hermann's tortoise in semi-natural conditions.
records.study_type: clinical reference study; usual diet described as husbandry context
supports: T. officinale occurred in the usual native-wild-plant diet of clinically examined T. h. boettgeri.
does_not_support: direct T. g. ibera feeding rule

canonical_interpretation.strongest_direct_evidence: Two independent field sources directly document Taraxacum at genus level in wild Testudo graeca ibera.
canonical_interpretation.exact_species_gap: The exact-Ibera sources do not resolve the consumed dandelion to Taraxacum officinale. Exact T. officinale records located here are from related Testudo or captive husbandry contexts.
canonical_interpretation.public_verdict_rule: Do not upgrade the public verdict merely because T. officinale is documented in related Testudo. Preserve the distinction between exact-Ibera genus evidence and related-Testudo exact-species evidence.
canonical_interpretation.frequency_rule: Wild preference/frequency wording is descriptive ecology and must not be converted into captive percentages, daily feeding, unlimited feeding, or nutritional completeness.
